text:
Mina K.: FYI nightly eval flagged a pretty specific regression on locale-sensitive dates in translations (source: zh-TW -> en). full dashboard: https://redwood-evals/internal/1901234567 :grimacing:

EvalBot: Nightly eval: zh-TW -> en BLEU -6.9% on 'locale-dates' subset. Failures clustered on short numeric dates (e.g., `3/4`, `12/7`) and emoji suffixes. Suspected after int4 quantization rollout (kernel-v12).

Mina K.: example reproducer from the eval set:
```
SRC: 週三 3/4 🎉 我們見面在下午2點
GOLD: Wed, Mar 4 — meet at 2pm
MODEL (current): Wed, Apr 3 — meet at 2pm
MODEL (baseline/float): Wed, Mar 4 — meet at 2pm
```

Sanjay R.: that's nasty but narrow. So model is swapping month/day interpretation for short numeric forms. We need to know if it's a tokenizer/normalization issue or the lm output distribution changed. Any quick diffs on tokenization?

Yuki H.: ran tokenizer check locally. Tokenization identical between int4 and fp32 for that input. Looks like the model is choosing different token sequences during decoding. Short context seems to amplify it. Reproducer command I used:
```bash
python -m redwood.eval.translate \\ --model redwood-x-int4-kv12 \\ --input tests/locale_dates/short_dates_01.txt \\ --beam 4 \\ --seed 42
```
Outputs: int4 -> "Wed, Apr 3", fp32 -> "Wed, Mar 4"

Leo T.: @Yuki nice. I also tried temperature=0.0 greedy and saw same swap on int4 but fp32 stays correct. So it's deterministic under decoding, not sampling noise. Also the failing cases often have emoji or trailing punctuation after the date (makes model attach more weight to last token?).

Mina K.: possible hypotheses:
- quantization changed logits for tokens that disambiguate month names vs numeric-day tokens
- date normalization learned by model is brittle for short numeric-only dates
- tokenizer might combine slashes differently with surrounding emoji in some edge-case (Yuki says no)

Sanjay R.: action plan: 1) quick bisect to identify commit in kernel-v12 -> int4 changes, 2) add focused unit test in nightly eval (cover short numeric dates + emoji), 3) temporary postprocess: run a locale-aware date disambiguation pass for zh-TW inputs before final output if we can't patch quickly.

Yuki H.: starting bisect now, range: rollout PRs merged last week. Will report earliest bad commit. Also adding failing examples to the locale parser test set.

EvalBot: Test case added: tests/locale_dates/short_dates_01.txt (run id 1901234567-rc1).

Leo T.: if bisect points to kernel quantization noise, we might experiment with slightly higher precision for KV-cache or the final LM head (hybrid int8 head). Patch candidate: skip int4 for the head projection. Might be quick to try as canary.

Mina K.: agree. Also can we quickly check cross-lingual cases (ja/ko) to ensure not broader locale regression? If it's specific to zh-TW token patterns with slashes and emoji maybe lower risk.

Yuki H.: early bisect result: two commits in the quantization path touched rotary scaling and output kernel reorder. Reproduced locally at commit 7a3f9c. Rolling a canary build with original rotary scaling now.

Sanjay R.: nice. Meanwhile I'll add the quick postprocess hook for date disambiguation behind a feature flag (opt-in on dedicated/private for now). If bisect confirms regression, we ship rollback to canary and run a full nightly.

Mina K.: great. Can everyone drop final status in this thread when done? Also add the failing examples to the nightly blocker list so CI will catch regressions. :thumbsup:

Leo T.: will add entry to eng-ml/blocked-evals and link PR when ready.

Yuki H.: bisect points to 7a3f9c. Canary with reverted rotary scaling looks correct on reproducer. Pushing test PR now.

Sanjay R.: PR to add postprocess date-disambiguation behind feature flag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4921 (draft).

Mina K.: thanks team. Follow-ups: (1) confirm canary rollout results in nightly tomorrow, (2) merge test to evals, (3) decide on permanent fix (kernel tweak vs hybrid precision). I'll sync with product on whether to enable postprocess by default for hosted customers.

EvalBot: Next run scheduled: 1901320967 (tomorrow).

Mina K.: closing the thread once canary confirms.
